pages.notes: Real <button> with aria-expanded/aria-controls and an accessible name; panel is a labelled region. Required action inferable from the accessibility tree alone. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.
Visually identical to the accessible variant but built from divs with a click handler; no ARIA, no accessible name, no tabindex. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.
Slide 1 is visible at load and has no sentinel. Slides 2-4 each fetch one sentinel on first reveal only. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.
Arrow controls are unlabeled divs; no ARIA, no tabindex. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.
Real <button> labelled 'Load more'; each of the two clicks appends one batch and fetches one sentinel. A third click is a no-op. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 PASSES under guard-removal.
Same behavior via a styled <span> with a click handler; no button role, no accessible name, no tabindex. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 PASSES under guard-removal.

Text sentinels live in a <template> and are absent from the rendered DOM until the trigger clones them. Real <button> with aria-expanded/aria-controls. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under text-guard-removal.

Text sentinels are in the DOM under display:none; the trigger is an unlabeled fade overlay div with no ARIA and no tabindex. guard_observable derived empirically: no resource sentinels and the text reveal only toggles a class, so no guard of either kind exists to observe.
Opens on real mouseover and on keyboard focus. Trigger is a <button> with aria-expanded/aria-haspopup; menu is a labelled list. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 PASSES under guard-removal.

Responds to mouseover only: no focus path, no click path, no ARIA, no tabindex. Verified: programmatic focus, Tab+Enter and a synthetic element.click() all fetch nothing; only mouseover opens it. Note that a real pointer click necessarily fires mouseover first, so a crawler using real mouse input will trigger this reveal incidentally when clicking the element. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 PASSES under guard-removal.

Page is >3000px tall; all three slots start below the fold. IntersectionObserver assembles each URL in JS on first intersection. No data-src, no srcset. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Page is >3000px tall. A batch is appended when the footer enters the viewport; exactly three batches then the observer disconnects. Terminates. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 PASSES under guard-removal. The batch counter is itself a structural guard: appendBatch is only called while appended < BATCHES.length and it increments before returning, so each batch index is fetched at most once and the observer disconnects after the third. Removing the fetchSentinel guard therefore changes nothing - this page is idempotent by construction, not by accident.

Attribute-name isolation pair: the sentinel URL is held in data-src. Identical to its partner page in every other respect - same images, same markup, same single click - so the difference in recall between the two is attributable to the attribute name alone. Browsertrix autofetch harvests data-src and srcset, and also any data-* attribute whose value starts with http, /, ./ or ../ (AutoFetcher.extractDataAttributes, browsertrix-behaviors src/autofetcher.ts:343-352), so it harvests data-lazy too: with autofetch enabled both pages are fetched without any click, and the pair isolates the attribute name only for crawlers that do not scan data-* values. expect_static_discoverable is true because the URL is in the served HTML by construction, which is the property under test; A4 is therefore not asserted, A3 still is. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Attribute-name isolation pair: the sentinel URL is held in data-lazy. Identical to its partner page in every other respect - same images, same markup, same single click - so the difference in recall between the two is attributable to the attribute name alone. Browsertrix autofetch harvests data-src and srcset, and also any data-* attribute whose value starts with http, /, ./ or ../ (AutoFetcher.extractDataAttributes, browsertrix-behaviors src/autofetcher.ts:343-352), so it harvests data-lazy too: with autofetch enabled both pages are fetched without any click, and the pair isolates the attribute name only for crawlers that do not scan data-* values. expect_static_discoverable is true because the URL is in the served HTML by construction, which is the property under test; A4 is therefore not asserted, A3 still is. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Toggle whose trigger is a div with role=button, an aria-label, aria-expanded/aria-controls and tabindex=0; handler attached with addEventListener. No cursor: pointer on the trigger or any ancestor, so a crawler that finds clickables by cursor style misses it; the role makes it findable from the accessibility tree. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Same toggle built from a plain div holding only an icon: no role, no accessible name, no tabindex, no onclick attribute; handler attached with addEventListener. No cursor: pointer on the trigger or any ancestor. Only a crawler that sees the registered click listener can find it. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Carousel whose real <button> 'Next slide' is in the DOM at load but whose click handler is attached 4 s after load, as a server-rendered page attaches handlers on hydration. A click before then does nothing. Hydration is simulated with a loading indicator that updates the DOM every 250 ms until the handler attaches (the corpus allows no non-sentinel requests, so the activity is DOM-only); a page that hydrates with no DOM or network activity at all would look quiet to a settle-on-quiet crawler. required_actions waits 4.5 s first. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Two same-origin iframes, each with an in-page anchor link (href="#answer-N") that reveals an answer and asks the page to fetch a sentinel. The hash change adds an entry to the session history the frames share with the page: a crawler that undoes it with history.back() can undo another frame's entry and wait for a popstate that never comes. The sentinel logic lives in the page (window.reveal), so mutations apply to it. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Gallery of links to full-size images (<a href="...large-0N.jpg">, another document) whose click handler cancels the navigation and loads the image into a viewer. A crawler that never clicks links to other documents misses all three; one that clicks links with a click listener, behind a navigation guard, recovers them. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

A client-side router that renders from the URL, also on popstate. Two navigation buttons and a router link push path routes (/pages/click/router-spa.html/<view>); the two reveal cards and a load-more list exist only in the home view. A crawler that clicks the navigation first must restore the route through a popstate: after one push and back() a forward entry exists, the next push leaves history.length unchanged, and a restore that only puts the URL back with replaceState leaves the router on the other view, so the home view is gone. Load more pushes ?page=N and appends one page with one sentinel; the router draws as many pages as the URL says, so a crawler that undoes ?page=1 gets page 0 redrawn and recovers only the first page. A 'Previous page' button at the top of the home view is aria-disabled, but its handler still pushes ?page=0, which the router draws as an empty page: a crawler that clicks disabled controls loses the cards and the results. The sort click replaces the path, so the original route cannot be traversed back to; it reveals no sentinel, since a route change is not a reveal. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Numbered pagination whose whole bar is rebuilt on every page change, so each button is a new node each time (as on BBC). Pages 2-4 each fetch one sentinel. A crawler that knows elements only by node identity keeps re-clicking the same page buttons; one that knows them by signature stops once revisiting reveals nothing. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Like React-Modal (gymshark): every click anywhere appends another empty, zero-size portal div with a click listener, ahead of three listener-only story controls. A crawler that clicks zero-size listener elements clicks portal after portal and never reaches the stories. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Load more whose button is rebuilt as a new node with the same markup after every batch; four batches, one sentinel each. A crawler that skips a re-rendered control it has seen must still continue while the control keeps revealing. Batches are one-way, so repeating the action cannot fetch a sentinel twice: guard_observable derived empirically: A6 PASSES under guard-removal.

Four identical 'Read more' buttons (same text and attributes) in four cards, each revealing a different sentinel. A signature without the element's position collapses them to one and clicks only the first. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Load more backed by a slow server: each click fetches the batch's data with serve.py's delay=800 parameter, then draws the batch and requests its image (the sentinel). Clicks while a batch is loading are ignored. Deliberately slower than the corpus's 200 ms reveal rule (spec section 4), hence the waits between clicks. A crawler that judges a click after a fixed 250 ms sees nothing new on the first click and stops; one that waits for the click's request and the DOM changes it brings recovers all four. Batches are one-way: guard_observable derived empirically: A6 PASSES under guard-removal.

Pure CSS menu: li:hover > .nav-menu { display: block }, no event handler anywhere on the page. Each menu row's thumbnail is a CSS background-image installed at load through CSSOM insertRule from assetUrl(), so no url() is in the served HTML and autofetch (which reads url() only inside @media rules) harvests nothing; the browser requests a thumbnail only once the menu renders. Synthetic mouse events do not set :hover, so only real pointer input reveals it. The first action hovers the h1 so the repeat passes leave and re-enter the menu. guard_observable derived empirically: sentinels are fetched by the style engine, so no page-JS guard exists to remove; A6 is exercised by script-fetch-css instead.

Two product tiles whose :hover rule sets a background-image (installed at load through CSSOM insertRule from assetUrl(), so no url() is in the served HTML). The tiles are plain divs with no listener, no ARIA and no tabindex: only a stylesheet scan can tell they react to hover, and only real pointer input sets :hover. Same layout and sentinel count as hover-js-imageswap, which reveals by mouseenter instead. guard_observable derived empirically: sentinels are fetched by the style engine, so no page-JS guard exists to remove; A6 is exercised by script-fetch-css instead.

Two product tiles; mouseenter swaps each tile's placeholder for its alternate image (the sentinel), mouseleave swaps back. Plain divs with no ARIA and no tabindex; the listener is the only signal. Same layout and sentinel count as hover-css-bgimage, so the pair isolates CSS :hover from a JS handler. The first action hovers the h1 so each repeat pass leaves and re-enters the tiles. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

Hover-intent menu: mouseenter starts a 300 ms timer, mouseleave cancels it, and the menu (whose rows load the sentinels) opens only when the timer completes. Deliberately slower than the corpus's 200 ms reveal rule (spec section 4), hence the wait: a crawler that moves on, or judges the hover, before 300 ms of continuous hover sees nothing. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.

A mouseenter menu whose 'Archives' row opens a submenu on its own mouseenter; the sentinels are the submenu's thumbnails and the top-level menu fetches nothing. The submenu trigger is hidden until the top-level menu is open, and the submenu sits inside its row, so it stays open only while the pointer travels through the parent chain: a crawler must hover the top-level item, then the row, while the menu is still open. guard_observable derived empirically: A6 FAILS under guard-removal.
